item.title: Sony India FY26 net profit rises 19% to ₹187 crore, revenue grows 0.85%
item.description: Consumer electronics maker Sony India's profit rose 19 per cent to Rs 186.88 crore in FY26, while its revenue from operations grew marginally by 0.85 per cent to Rs 7,917.99 crore, according to regulatory filings. Total income, including other income, increased 1.32 per cent to Rs 8,022.73 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to financial data accessed through business intelligence platform Tofler. Sony India, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Japanese technology major Sony Corporation, had reported a profit of Rs 157.03 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 7,851.08 crore in FY25. India is Sony's fourth-largest market globally, after the US, China and Japan. The company aims to make India its third-largest market worldwide, overtaking its home market Japan. Sony India's advertising and promotional expenses declined marginally to Rs 182.58 crore in FY26 from Rs 183.71 crore a year earlier. item.title: J&K Bank Q2 result: Profit climbs 10.6% to ₹546 cr, asset quality improves
item.description: Jammu and Kashmir Bank on Thursday reported a 10.6 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 546.36 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, driven by earnings growth and improvement in asset quality. The bank earned Rs 494.11 crore net profit in the year-ago period. Sequentially, its profits surged 28.8 per cent from Rs 424.18 crore in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, a bank spokesperson said. The bank announced the financial results after its Board of Directors reviewed and approved the quarterly and half-yearly figures at a meeting held at its corporate headquarters here on Thursday. Its net interest income rose 5 per cent during the quarter to Rs 1,502 crore. The lender's other income more than doubled to Rs 314.90 crore from Rs 153.76 cr a year ago. For the first half of the current fiscal year, the bank's operating expenditure grew 1.5 per cent, and its operating profit rose over 15 per cent to Rs 1,492 crore. item.title: BCGCL begins construction work on ₹25,000 crore coal gasification project
item.description: Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (BCGCL), the joint venture of Coal India Ltd (CIL) and BHEL, has started ground construction activities for its Rs 25,000 crore coal gasification project in Odisha, with most of the tenders awarded, its Managing Director Peeyush Kumar said on Thursday. The development assumes significance in the wake of the country's push to build 100 million tonne of coal gasification capacity by 2030 under the National Coal Gasification Mission, aimed at converting coal into chemicals and bringing down the import dependence on products such as LNG, urea, ammonia and methanol. "We are going ahead with the joint venture of BHEL and Coal India, which is BCGCL....I am happy to share that we have started ground construction activities... Most of the tenders have been awarded and construction has started," Kumar said during the 17th Edition of Gasification India 2026 organised by Mission Energy Foundation.
